Based on the chest X-ray findings presented in Figures 4a and 4b, what is the most likely diagnosis for the vascular anomaly causing the patient's symptoms, considering the presence of a retrocardiac tubular opacity?

A) Bronchopulmonary sequestration
B) Systemic arterialization of the left lung lower lobe without sequestration
C) Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation
D) Chronic inflammatory disease of the lung with hypertrophied bronchial artery
E) Normal anatomical variation with no clinical significance
F) Congenital pulmonary venolobar syndrome
